stem: In the Mahabharata's frame story, who recites the epic at King Janamejaya's snake sacrifice?
options: Sanjaya, the blind king's charioteer
Shuka, the son of the sage Vyasa
Vaishampayana, a disciple of Vyasa
Narada, the wandering divine sage
why: At Janamejaya's snake sacrifice, Vyasa's disciple Vaishampayana tells the story of the king's ancestors; Sauti later retells what he heard there to the sages of the Naimisha forest. Mahabharata, Adi Parva.
source: Mahabharata, Adi Parva (Anukramanika and Astika Parvas)

es.stem: En el relato marco del Mahabharata, ¿quién recita la épica en el sacrificio de serpientes del rey Janamejaya?
options: Sanjaya, el auriga del rey ciego
Shuka, el hijo del gran sabio Vyasa
Vaishampayana, discípulo de Vyasa
Narada, el sabio divino errante
es.why: En el sacrificio de serpientes de Janamejaya, Vaishampayana, discípulo de Vyasa, narra la historia de los antepasados del rey; después Sauti repite lo que oyó allí a los sabios del bosque de Naimisha. Mahabharata, Adi Parva.

stem: In the Mahabharata's Adi Parva, why does Devavrata come to be called Bhishma?
options: for his fearsome duel with his teacher Parashurama
for his terrible vow to give up throne and marriage
for slaying the gandharva who had killed his brother
for the dread curse he laid on the house of Drupada
why: To win Satyavati for his father Shantanu, Devavrata renounces the throne and vows lifelong celibacy; the gods shower flowers and call him Bhishma, 'the terrible one', for that vow. Mahabharata, Adi Parva, Sambhava Parva.

es.stem: En el Adi Parva del Mahabharata, ¿por qué a Devavrata se le llega a llamar Bhishma?
options: por su temible duelo contra su propio maestro Parashurama
por su terrible voto de dejar el trono y el matrimonio
por matar al gandharva que había matado a su hermano
por la maldición que lanzó sobre la casa de Drupada
es.why: Para conseguir a Satyavati para su padre Shantanu, Devavrata renuncia al trono y hace voto de celibato de por vida; los dioses lo cubren de flores y lo llaman Bhishma, 'el terrible', por ese voto. Mahabharata, Adi Parva, Sambhava Parva.

stem: In the Mahabharata's Adi Parva, why is Dhritarashtra born blind?
options: Shantanu's grief fell upon the unborn child
a sage cursed the Kuru line for Bhishma's vow
Gandhari's father laid a curse on the house
Ambika shut her eyes in fear when Vyasa came
why: Vyasa is called to father heirs for the childless dead king; Ambika, frightened by his looks, keeps her eyes shut, and Vyasa says her son will be born blind. Mahabharata, Adi Parva, Sambhava Parva.

es.stem: En el Adi Parva del Mahabharata, ¿por qué Dhritarashtra nace ciego?
options: el dolor de Shantanu cayó sobre el niño por nacer
un sabio maldijo el linaje kuru por el voto de Bhishma
el padre de Gandhari lanzó una maldición sobre la casa
Ambika cerró los ojos por miedo cuando llegó Vyasa
es.why: Llaman a Vyasa para dar herederos al rey que murió sin hijos; Ambika, asustada por su aspecto, mantiene los ojos cerrados, y Vyasa anuncia que su hijo nacerá ciego. Mahabharata, Adi Parva, Sambhava Parva.

stem: In the Mahabharata's Sabha Parva, Krishna had promised Shishupala's mother to pardon how many of her son's offenses?
options: 100 offenses
1,000 offenses
108 offenses
500 offenses
why: At the birth of Shishupala, his mother, Krishna's aunt, begged him to spare her son, and Krishna promised to forgive a hundred offenses; at the Rajasuya the count runs out. Mahabharata, Sabha Parva, Sisupala-badha Parva.

es.stem: En el Sabha Parva del Mahabharata, Krishna le había prometido a la madre de Shishupala perdonar ¿cuántas ofensas de su hijo?
options: 100 ofensas
1000 ofensas
108 ofensas
500 ofensas
es.why: Al nacer Shishupala, su madre, tía de Krishna, le rogó que perdonara a su hijo, y Krishna prometió perdonarle cien ofensas; en el Rajasuya la cuenta se agota. Mahabharata, Sabha Parva, Sisupala-badha Parva.

stem: In the Vana Parva, Shiva gives Arjuna the Pashupata weapon with a warning about its use. If Arjuna later faced a weak, ordinary human foe, what would that warning require?
options: use it only after first warning the foe
use it if the foe had struck the first blow
use it once Indra had given his own consent
hold it back and not hurl it at such a foe
why: Shiva tells Arjuna the Pashupata must not be hurled at men without great cause, and that loosed on a weaker foe it could destroy the world. Mahabharata, Vana Parva, Kairata Parva.

es.stem: En el Vana Parva, Shiva le da a Arjuna el arma Pashupata con una advertencia sobre su uso. Si Arjuna se enfrentara más tarde a un enemigo humano común y débil, ¿qué exigiría esa advertencia?
options: usarla solo después de avisar al enemigo
usarla si el enemigo dio el primer golpe
usarla cuando Indra haya dado su permiso
contenerse y no lanzarla contra él
es.why: Shiva le dice a Arjuna que la Pashupata no debe lanzarse contra hombres sin una gran causa, y que lanzada contra un enemigo más débil podría destruir el mundo. Mahabharata, Vana Parva, Kairata Parva.

stem: In the Mahabharata's Sabha Parva, why must Jarasandha be dealt with before Yudhishthira can perform the Rajasuya?
options: he holds many kings captive and blocks the rite
he has seized the Kuru capital at Hastinapura
he has stolen the horse meant for the great sacrifice
he has sworn to kill Yudhishthira at the rite
why: Krishna explains that Jarasandha holds many kings prisoner and no Rajasuya is possible while he stands; after Bhima kills him in a wrestling match, the kings are freed and Jarasandha's son is put on the throne. Mahabharata, Sabha Parva, Jarasandha-vadha Parva.
source: Mahabharata, Sabha Parva, Rajasuyarambha and Jarasandha-vadha Parvas

es.stem: En el Sabha Parva del Mahabharata, ¿por qué hay que enfrentar a Jarasandha antes de que Yudhishthira pueda celebrar el Rajasuya?
options: tiene presos a muchos reyes y bloquea el rito
se ha apoderado de la capital kuru, Hastinapura
ha robado el caballo destinado al gran sacrificio
ha jurado matar a Yudhishthira durante el rito
es.why: Krishna explica que Jarasandha tiene presos a muchos reyes y que no habrá Rajasuya mientras él siga en pie; cuando Bhima lo mata en una lucha cuerpo a cuerpo, los reyes quedan libres y el hijo de Jarasandha sube al trono. Mahabharata, Sabha Parva, Jarasandha-vadha Parva.

stem: In the Mahabharata's opening frame, how does King Janamejaya's snake sacrifice come to an end?
why: The young sage Astika, nephew of the snake king Vasuki, so pleases Janamejaya that the king offers him any gift; Astika asks that the sacrifice stop, and the king keeps his word, sparing Takshaka. Mahabharata, Adi Parva, Astika Parva.

rubric.point: Names Astika, or a young sage or brahmin related to the snakes, as the one who stops it. Saying only that 'the gods stopped it' does not count.
Says he does it by asking for the end of the sacrifice as the gift the king has promised him, and the king keeps his word. 'He persuaded the king' without the promised boon counts as partly.
Mentions that Takshaka, the snake who killed Janamejaya's father Parikshit, is spared, or that the epic is told at this sacrifice (optional, strengthens).

es.stem: En el marco inicial del Mahabharata, ¿cómo llega a su fin el sacrificio de serpientes del rey Janamejaya?
es.why: El joven sabio Astika, sobrino del rey serpiente Vasuki, complace tanto a Janamejaya que el rey le ofrece cualquier regalo; Astika pide que se detenga el sacrificio, y el rey cumple su palabra y perdona a Takshaka. Mahabharata, Adi Parva, Astika Parva.

stem: In the Mahabharata's Sabha Parva, after the dice game, what boons does Draupadi ask of Dhritarashtra, and why does she refuse a third?
why: Draupadi asks first for Yudhishthira's freedom, then for the freedom of the other four brothers with their weapons and chariots; she declines a third, saying a woman of the warrior class may ask only two and her husbands can win back the rest by their own deeds. Mahabharata, Sabha Parva, Dyuta Parva.

rubric.point: Says she asks for the freedom of her husbands: Yudhishthira first, then the other four (with their weapons and chariots). Naming only one of the two boons counts as partly.
Says she refuses a third because a kshatriya (warrior-class) woman should ask no more than two, or because her freed husbands can regain the rest by their own deeds. Either reason counts.
Mentions that she asks Yudhishthira's freedom so her son will not be called a slave's son, or that Dhritarashtra acts after ill omens in the hall (optional, strengthens).

es.stem: En el Sabha Parva del Mahabharata, después del juego de dados, ¿qué dones le pide Draupadi a Dhritarashtra, y por qué rechaza un tercero?
es.why: Draupadi pide primero la libertad de Yudhishthira y luego la de los otros cuatro hermanos con sus armas y carros; rechaza un tercer don diciendo que una mujer de la clase guerrera solo puede pedir dos y que sus esposos recuperarán lo demás por sus propios actos. Mahabharata, Sabha Parva, Dyuta Parva.
